references.text: Matthew's parallel account of the feeding of the five thousand, where it mentions that there were about five thousand men, besides women and children.
Mark's parallel account where Jesus instructs the disciples to have the people sit down in groups, by companies, and they sat down in groups of a hundred and fifty.
Mark notes that there were five thousand men who ate the loaves, corresponding to the number in Luke 9:14.
John's parallel account where Jesus says 'Have the people sit down', and it mentions that there were about five thousand men.

Jethro advised Moses to organize the people into groups of a thousand, a hundred, fifty, and ten – a similar principle of organizing large crowds into manageable units, just as Jesus organized the five thousand in groups of fifty.
The organization of Israel's army into companies and divisions, illustrating the principle of arranging large crowds into smaller units.

The following verse where Jesus takes the five loaves and the two fish, looks up to heaven, blesses them, breaks them, and gives them to the disciples to distribute – the miracle itself that followed after organizing the people into groups.
Elisha's miracle of feeding a hundred men with twenty barley loaves, where there was also food left over – an Old Testament precursor to Jesus' feeding miracle.
